newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Beijing to have last word on migrants to Hong Kong.
newsitem.headline: Beijing to have last word on migrants to Hong Kong.

text.p: China will have the last word on who can migrate from the mainland to Hong Kong after Beijing takes the colony back from Britain on July 1, a senior Chinese official was quoted as saying on Wednesday.

Chen Ziying, a deputy director of Beijing's Hong Kong and Macau Affairs Office, was quoted by the South China Morning Post in a despatch from Beijing as saying it would be difficult for the post-colonial government to deal with the issue.
"How can it know who is qualified or not," Chen said, adding that the Special Administrative Region, as Hong Kong will be known, could not refuse any legal migrants from the mainland.

Hong Kong a small, crowded territory of 6.4 million people, is reverting to China under a 1984 treaty allowing it to keep its capitalist system for a further 50 years and to enjoy a high degree of autonomy.
In negotiations on the handover details, Britain and China have failed to agree so far on the burning issue of who can have the right of abode in Hong Kong and on what terms.
Many in Hong Kong fear that Beijing will allow mainland migrants to swamp the territory.
Chen also said China had to work out how to handle a likely flood of demands by mainland Chinese to visit Hong Kong as tourists after the handover.
"It is understandable that many Chinese people want to go to Hong Kong to have a look after it has been administered by Britain for more than 100 years," Chen said.
"But it is a small place. We have to find a way to allow them to have a look, while ensuring the territory will not be disturbed," he said.
He said this did not include Chinese officials who needed to make working visits to the territory, for whom he said entry would be a mere formality.
